# Generated by /feature-spec
# Feature: Jarvis serve-nats Socket-Liveness Watchdog
# Stack: generic
# Assumptions: 7 (see jarvis-serve-nats-watchdog_assumptions.yaml)
# Generated: 2026-08-11T09:30:00Z

@jarvis-serve-nats-watchdog
Feature: Jarvis serve-nats Socket-Liveness Watchdog
  As an operator of the jarvis Slack door
  I want the real serve-nats ingress service versioned, watched for staleness, and correctly registered
  So that a silently stale Slack door is detected and announced even when no operator is present

  Background:
    Given the jarvis Slack door is served by the serve-nats service

  # ── GROUP A: Key Examples ──

  # Why: Core versioning path — the repository must carry the real Slack door service definition, not the wrong one
  # [ASSUMPTION: confidence=high] The running serve-nats service is a user-scoped service that can be captured as a versioned definition
  @key-example @smoke
  Scenario: The real Slack door service definition is versioned in the repository
    Given the running serve-nats service definition exists only on the host
    When the service definition is captured into the operations area of the repository
    Then the versioned definition should match the behaviour of the running service
    And the versioned definition should be scoped to the operator's user session

  # Why: The install step is what makes the versioned definition deployable — it mirrors the existing frontdoor install pattern
  @key-example
  Scenario: The coordinator install step deploys the versioned service definition
    Given the serve-nats service definition is versioned in the repository
    When the coordinator follows the documented install step
    Then the serve-nats service should be installed as a user service on the host
    And the install documentation should follow the same pattern as the existing frontdoor service

  # Why: A healthy door must not raise noise — silence from the watchdog means health, so false alerts destroy trust
  @key-example
  Scenario: A healthy Slack door raises no alert
    Given the serve-nats journal shows recent subscription activity
    When the watchdog checks the door
    Then no alert should be posted
    And the watchdog should record that the door is healthy

  # Why: The reason the feature exists — a quiet door with nobody watching must announce itself
  # [ASSUMPTION: confidence=medium] The service journal contains detectable socket and subscription activity patterns
  @key-example @smoke
  Scenario: A stale Slack door triggers a Slack alert
    Given the serve-nats journal shows no subscription activity within the staleness window
    When the watchdog checks the door
    # [ASSUMPTION: confidence=medium] An outbound Slack notification path is available to the watchdog
    Then an alert should be posted to Slack
    And the alert should say the Slack door has gone quiet

  # Why: Operational truth — the register must name the real door so responders act on the right service
  @key-example @smoke
  Scenario: The O-30 register names serve-nats as the Slack door
    # [ASSUMPTION: confidence=high] The O-30 register is an editable row-based operational document
    Given the O-30 register row names langgraph dev as the Slack door
    When the register row is corrected
    Then the register row should name serve-nats as the Slack door
    And every other field in the register row should be unchanged

  # ── GROUP B: Boundary Conditions ──

  # Why: Just-inside boundary — activity inside the staleness window keeps the door healthy
  @boundary
  Scenario Outline: Recent activity inside the staleness window raises no alert
    # [ASSUMPTION: confidence=low] The staleness window is 15 minutes without subscription activity
    Given the last subscription activity was <elapsed> ago
    When the watchdog checks the door
    Then no alert should be posted

    Examples:
      | elapsed    |
      | 1 minute   |
      | 14 minutes |
      | 15 minutes |

  # Why: Just-outside boundary — the first moment past the window must alert
  @boundary @negative
  Scenario: Activity just outside the staleness window triggers an alert
    Given the last subscription activity was 16 minutes ago
    When the watchdog checks the door
    Then an alert should be posted to Slack

  # Why: Just-inside boundary — a still-stale door inside the reminder interval must not flood the channel
  @boundary
  Scenario: A continuing outage inside the reminder interval is not re-announced
    # [ASSUMPTION: confidence=low] A continuing outage is re-announced no more than once per hour
    Given an alert for the current outage was posted 59 minutes ago
    And the door is still stale
    When the watchdog checks the door
    Then no additional alert should be posted

  # Why: Just-outside boundary — a long-running outage must be re-announced so it cannot be forgotten
  @boundary
  Scenario: A continuing outage past the reminder interval is re-announced
    Given an alert for the current outage was posted 61 minutes ago
    And the door is still stale
    When the watchdog checks the door
    Then a reminder alert should be posted to Slack

  # ── GROUP C: Negative Cases ──

  # Why: The watchdog must not silently succeed when its own evidence source is missing
  @negative
  Scenario: The watchdog reports when the service journal cannot be read
    Given the serve-nats journal is not readable
    When the watchdog checks the door
    Then the watchdog should report that it cannot determine door health
    And the outcome should not be recorded as healthy

  # Why: A failure of the failure-reporter must not be swallowed
  @negative
  Scenario: A failed alert delivery is recorded and retried
    Given the door is stale
    And Slack alert delivery fails
    When the watchdog attempts to post the alert
    Then the delivery failure should be recorded on the host
    And the alert should be attempted again on the next check

  # Why: The wrong service must no longer masquerade as the Slack door in the repository
  @negative
  Scenario: The frontdoor service definition is no longer presented as the Slack door
    Given the repository previously presented the frontdoor service as the Slack door
    When the versioned service definitions are reviewed
    Then the serve-nats definition should be identified as the Slack door
    And the frontdoor definition should not be described as the Slack door

  # ── GROUP D: Edge Cases ──

  # Why: The silent-death case is the observed failure — process alive, subscription dead
  @edge-case @regression
  Scenario: A running door with a dead subscription is still detected as stale
    Given the serve-nats service is running
    And the journal shows no subscription activity within the staleness window
    When the watchdog checks the door
    Then an alert should be posted to Slack

  # Why: A fully stopped service is also a quiet door — detection must not require the service to be running
  @edge-case
  Scenario: A stopped door service is detected and alerted
    Given the serve-nats service is not running
    When the watchdog checks the door
    Then an alert should be posted to Slack
    And the alert should say the door service is not running

  # Why: Recovery must close the episode so alerts describe reality
  @edge-case
  Scenario: A recovered door closes the outage episode
    Given an outage alert was previously posted
    And the journal now shows fresh subscription activity
    When the watchdog checks the door
    # [ASSUMPTION: confidence=low] A recovery notice is posted when the door returns
    Then a recovery notice should be posted to Slack
    And the outage episode should be closed

  # Why: The alert path must not depend on the inbound door it is reporting on
  @edge-case
  Scenario: An alert is delivered while the inbound Slack door is down
    Given the serve-nats subscription is stale
    And the outbound Slack alert path is available
    When the watchdog checks the door
    Then the alert should be delivered through the outbound path
```

# Feature Spec Summary: Jarvis serve-nats Socket-Liveness Watchdog

**Stack**: generic
**Generated**: 2026-08-11T09:30:00Z
**Scenarios**: 16 total (3 smoke, 1 regression)
**Assumptions**: 7 total (2 high / 2 medium / 3 low confidence)
**Review required**: Yes

## Scope

This specification covers the jarvis Slack door liveness programme: versioning the real serve-nats service definition into the repository with a coordinator install step matching the existing frontdoor pattern, a watchdog that reads the service journal for socket/subscription staleness and posts a Slack alert when the door goes quiet, and correcting the O-30 register row to name serve-nats — not langgraph dev — as the Slack door. Scope is ops files and a watchdog script only: no app source changes, no compose deploy, and jarvis is not a DCL venue.

## Scenario Counts by Category

| Category | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Key examples (@key-example) | 5 |
| Boundary conditions (@boundary) | 4 |
| Negative cases (@negative) | 4 |
| Edge cases (@edge-case) | 4 |

## Deferred Items

None. All four groups are included from the approved product documentation.

## Open Assumptions (low confidence)

- ASSUM-005 — staleness window is 15 minutes without subscription activity (the quiet window is an explicit open question)
- ASSUM-006 — continuing outages are re-announced no more than once per hour
- ASSUM-007 — a recovery notice is posted when the door returns to health

## Integration with /feature-plan

This summary can be passed to `/feature-plan` as a context file:

    /feature-plan "Jarvis serve-nats Socket-Liveness Watchdog" --context features/jarvis-serve-nats-watchdog/jarvis-serve-nats-watchdog_summary.md
```
